This is the course website for {{< var course.number >}}, *{{< var course.title >}}*, taught at [{{< var university.name >}}]({{< var university.url >}}) in the [{{< var department.name >}}]({{< var department.url >}}) in {{< var course.semester >}}.

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/), and the source is available [on GitHub]({{< var course.github >}}). Corrections and suggestions are welcome --- use the "Edit this page" or "Report an issue" links in the right margin, or open an issue directly.

## Credit

Course materials are by {{< var instructor.name_no_title >}} unless otherwise noted, and are licensed [CC-BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en). You are free to reuse and adapt them with attribution under the same license.

The site design derives from earlier offerings of this course and of BEE 4750/5750.

Several elements of the course's structure are borrowed and adapted with thanks:

- The four-step generative loop that organizes the course is adapted from Richard McElreath's *Statistical Rethinking* ([doi:10.1201/9780429029608](https://doi.org/10.1201/9780429029608)), without its Bayesian commitment.
- The homework assignment format --- lettered sub-parts with individual point values, an agenda stating what is being practiced explicitly and implicitly, and instructions on the *form* of an answer --- is adapted from [Cosma Shalizi's](https://www.stat.cmu.edu/~cshalizi/) homework assignments for 36-401 and 36-402 at Carnegie Mellon.

## Accessibility

If you encounter any part of this site that is inaccessible to you, please let me know at [{{< var instructor.email >}}](mailto:{{< var instructor.email >}}) and I will fix it.
